lessons.title: One-Sided Limits and When a Limit Exists
Harder Limits: Conjugates and Common Denominators
Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes
The Precise Definition of a Limit

atoms.objective: Define the limit of a function at a point informally and read it from a graph.
Define one-sided limits and use the existence test: a two-sided limit exists exactly when both one-sided limits exist and agree.
Compute limits of polynomial and rational functions by algebraic simplification, including limits at a hole.
Compute limits with indeterminate 0/0 forms by rationalizing with a conjugate and by combining compound fractions.
State the definition of continuity at a point and determine where a function is continuous from its formula or graph.
State and apply the intermediate value theorem to prove the existence of roots and intermediate values.
Evaluate limits at infinity for rational functions and identify horizontal asymptotes from end behaviour.
Analyse infinite limits by sign and identify vertical asymptotes, distinguishing divergence from a limit.
State the epsilon-delta definition of a limit and prove a linear limit by constructing delta in terms of epsilon.
